requiredNextAction: None outstanding. The ruling of 12 September 2026 closed findings 1, 6-13, 21, 24, 25, 28 and 19 as permanently unrecoverable, and finding 56 is fixed and verified in production. Two standing rules carry forward from this cycle: a future payroll defect is a NEW finding numbered from 57 onward and is never attributed to a closed number, and the next audit cycle writes its findings document into docs/production-audits/automated-payroll/ BEFORE its first fix pull request, not after its last one.
managerSummary: SCORE MEANING: 7.7 is not a quality rating of the payroll module. It is the share of the audit's findings this repository can account for - 43 of 56. It measures the RECORD, not the code. THE SCORE DID NOT MOVE WHEN THE FOURTEEN WERE CLOSED, and that is deliberate: closing them settled what is OWED, not what is KNOWN. A ruling cannot recover information that no longer exists, and a record that rewarded itself for deciding to stop looking would be worse than the gap it papered over. Cycle 1 ran 10-12 September 2026 and numbered 55 findings: 39 fixed with evidence anyone can check, 2 (30 and 36) claimed closed by earlier work that is not named anywhere, 1 (finding 19) mentioned only in passing, and 13 - findings 1, 6 to 13, 21, 24, 25 and 28 - appearing nowhere at all. Cycle 2 ran on 12 September 2026 because those 13 could not be recovered, and re-examined the module empirically instead. It found one new High finding: the only payroll-batch delete path the application uses switched off all three of the database guards that exist to stop a closed month being deleted, and then ignored the status it had just read. Every batch in production was in the protected state - 3 approved, 5 locked, 896 salary records between them - so nothing was legitimately deletable and everything was deletable, behind a single browser confirm, with no point-in-time recovery behind it. That is fixed and verified in production. THE OWNER RULED ON 12 SEPTEMBER 2026 that the fourteen findings nobody can account for - the 13 with no trace, plus finding 19 - are CLOSED as permanently unrecoverable. Closed is not fixed: nothing is claimed about what they contained, and if one of them described a live defect it is still live with no description to search for. That exposure is now an accepted residual risk rather than an open piece of work. The module therefore has no outstanding audit item. The severity counts below are a floor, not a total: they record only what a merged pull request stated in words, plus finding 56.

topBusinessRisks.risk: Fourteen findings are closed without anyone knowing what they were
topBusinessRisks.businessImpact: Findings 1, 6-13, 21, 24, 25, 28 and 19 were closed on 12 September 2026 as permanently unrecoverable. Nobody can say whether they were fixed, dismissed, folded into another finding, or dropped. If any of them touched money, the defect may still be live in payroll today and there is no description of it to look for. This is an accepted residual risk, not a resolved one.
topBusinessRisks.requiredAction: Treat it as accepted and do not re-litigate it - the decision is made and recorded in the audit ledger. Any payroll defect found from now on is a NEW finding, numbered from 57 onward, and is never attributed to a closed number.

topBusinessRisks.risk: A guard that the application disarms is invisible to everyone who trusts it
topBusinessRisks.businessImpact: Finding 56 was a trigger doing exactly its job while the one code path that mattered switched it off on every call. Anyone reading the schema would have concluded a closed month was protected. The same shape can exist anywhere a bypass flag was added for a legitimate cascade.
topBusinessRisks.requiredAction: When a migration adds a bypass for a guard, the function that sets it must re-assert the rule itself. DONE for the whole schema as of 12 September 2026: it holds exactly two such flags. request.phx_allow_salary_batch_delete was finding 56. request.phx_allow_terminal_employee_reactivation came back CLEAN - it is read only by the employees reactivation trigger and is set by nothing that ships: no database function, no migration, no application code, no role or database default, and no path a client can reach through PostgREST. The guard is armed on every route that exists, confirmed by a rolled-back probe on production. Apply the standard to any bypass added from now on.

topBusinessRisks.risk: An audit whose findings document is written last loses findings
topBusinessRisks.businessImpact: Cycle 1's findings existed only as code comments and pull-request descriptions for three days. Fourteen went missing in that window and are now closed permanently because of it. The cost of writing the document last was fourteen findings.
topBusinessRisks.requiredAction: Every future cycle writes its findings document into docs/production-audits/<module>/ before its first fix pull request. Cycle 2 followed that order; keep it.

topBusinessRisks.risk: The primary checkout is not a valid audit surface
topBusinessRisks.businessImpact: It was 14 commits stale at the start of cycle 2 and still held a file a merged ruling had deleted. An audit run there produces findings about code that does not ship, and fixes for problems nobody has.
topBusinessRisks.requiredAction: Confirm the surface against origin/main before reading a line of code, in every future cycle.
